newsitem.title: CANADA: Rain slows southern Alberta crop harvest - Albert Ag.
newsitem.headline: Rain slows southern Alberta crop harvest - Albert Ag.

text.p: Spring crop harvest should be general in the southern third of Alberta's grainbelt once the moisture from recent rains dries out, Alberta Agriculture's crop report for the week of August 11 said.
"The north still needs two to three weeks of good sunny weather to progress some late seeded crops," wrote Matthew Machielse, Alberta Agriculture's senior market analyst.
Rain held up operations late in the week as most regions reported good coverage between 0.5 to two inches.
South Alberta's harvest was verging on becoming general. Foremost crop district saw hail over a wide swath.
Central Alberta's eastern crops were being swathed as severe drought stress progressed crops rapidly. The region will be facing a feed deficit due to poor silage crops and no second cut hay crops.
Northeast Alberta canola swathing was 15 to 20 percent done and feed supplies were reported to be more than adequate.
Northwest Alberta had yet to start swathing except for early seeded barley and polish canola.
Peace River Valley saw more rain which slowed forage seed harvest.
